scope: Isolated local gamma reflex/reset pair and high-gamma motor/clear adapters using native ARM cell updates. Explicit sparse-connectivity, initial-phase and coupling assumptions; not the device compiler or an FPGA-equivalence test.
result: All twelve cases responded to one- and two-cue stimulation and returned to silence after stimulation ended. Readout bursts ranged from two to seven modeled steps. These checks do not identify an optimal TNorm.
schedule: 1200 steps per case: one cue at steps 50–349, no cue at 350–549, two cues at 550–849, no cue at 850–1199. Stimuli sampled every 1 or 3 steps. Baseline checked before 50; late silence checked from 1000.
variation: Six explicit initialization/coupling/membrane-floor combinations, each with two input sampling intervals.
limitations: One local circuit, with the same reflex/reset/output relationships as each shipped leg. Gait pathways, flexion competition, REST/STOP dynamics and STDP3 are excluded from this sensitivity harness; public graph and mocked runtime tests cover the separate structural and command contracts.
Connectivity and phase evolution are explicit local assumptions. A compiled device image can behave differently. Native cell updates alone do not establish complete runtime equivalence.
No Webots physics, ground contact, mechanical load, transport latency or servo completion was simulated.
Bistable output readouts are not internal neuron telemetry. No live saturation, dopamine firing or learning effect is established.
